newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Trelleborg H1 as expected but eyes on change.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Trelleborg H1 as expected but eyes on change.

text.p: Swedish mining and industrial rubber company Trelleborg on Tuesday posted a half year report slightly above expectations, while the market continued to focus on the changing shape of the cash-rich, restructured company.

Trelleborg posted a profit after financial items of 2.0 billion crowns ($249.7 million), against 657 million crowns a year ago, but this included a 1.46 billion crown capital gain from selling 55.1 percent of mining unit Boliden, now Toronto listed.
The market had expected a profit of 2.16 billion crowns including the capital gain, which was slightly below expectations.
Trelleborg pointed out that its operating profit, including associated interests but without capital gains or provisions, rose by 170 million crowns to 733 million crowns.

"The report was about in line with expectations although there could have been some disappointment that the profit development only came from newly acquired companies, not the underlying business," Nordiska Fondkommission analyst Claes Vikbladh said.
"But what most people are waiting to see now is when Trelleborg will hive off its Trelltrade businesses and what it will do with all the cash it is sitting on."
The only item that was a slight surprise was provisions of 159 million crowns for a sulphuric acid plant in the U.S. that has suffered industrial problems over the past year.
Trelleborg reported sales of 11.82 billion crowns for the six months against 10.54 billion crowns a year ago.
It repeated forecasts for a better 1997 result.
"We estimate that the full year result for 1997, excluding restructuring costs, will be better than in 1996," the company said in a statement.

Trelleborg has embarked on a process to sell off parts of its business to concentrate on industrial rubber operations, Trelleborg Industri, that reported a 44 percent rise in sales to 3.33 billion crowns in the first half as a result of acquisitions and favourable exchange rate movements.
"But I think Trelleborg still has to convince investors that the investments they are doing in the industrial rubber division are really going to create value over time," one Stockholm analyst said.
"I think some people are a bit sceptical as industrial rubber has low margins."
As part of its streamlining, in July this year Trelleborg sold 55.1 percent of wholly owned mining unit Boliden through an initial public offering in Canada.
The market is also expecting it to sell off the various units in its Trelltrade wholesale metals division, although this may wait until the Swedish construction market picks up.
"I think they will be a 100-percent industrial rubber company in the next two to three years," analyst Christofer Sjogren from Carnegie told Reuters.
"I think they will be looking at making some rubber acquisitions this autumn."
But the cash pile was likely to give some boost to shareholders.
"I think shareholders could look forward to dividends increasing this year," said Vikbladh. "It has always been the company's policy to distribute a large part of earnings to shareholders."
Trelleborg share price was unmoved by the report. It ended 0.5 crowns higher at 128 crowns.
-- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1045 ($ = 8.01 Swedish Crowns)
